text:
New Jersey needed this one. Two straight losses, and a recent night when Connor Hellebuyck was pulled after what CBS Sports called a disastrous first period, had the spotlight on the Devils' new goalie. On Monday he only needed 19 of them, and his team did the rest in a 3-2 win over Columbus.

The Devils built the lead early. Timo Meier scored at 4:59, staying hot, with Jack Hughes and Connor Brown assisting, and Brenden Dillon's slap shot from distance, a 3% chance, made it 2-0 at 8:12. Charlie Coyle cut it to one on Zach Werenski's feed late in the first, Brown restored the two-goal cushion at 14:41 of the second, and Mikael Pyyhtia answered short-handed with 14 seconds left in the period. Jack Williams picked up his first NHL point on that goal.

New Jersey earned it. The Devils had the better even-strength chances, 2.34 to 1.22 in expected goals, owned the second period, and deserved to win 64% of the replays of this game's shots. Cam Talbot kept Columbus close, including a stop on Nico Hischier's best look in the second. Hellebuyck finished right at expectation, 2 goals on 1.99 expected, which is what a team in a skid wants from its goalie: no drama.

Brown is the quiet story. He had a goal, an assist and four shots in 20:18, a few days after his comments about Connor McDavid drew headlines. Werenski played 30:54 for Columbus and put six shots on goal, carrying the load he has carried all season.

The two teams meet again Wednesday, per Mike Fink, so Columbus does not have to wait long for an answer. The Blue Jackets also lost Mathieu Olivier to an upper-body injury, per Daily Faceoff, a worry for a forward group that now includes Matthew Knies, the former Maple Leaf.
headline: Devils snap skid behind Meier, Brown and a busy first
